title: CarTrade Tech Ltd - 543333 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: CarTrade Q2 FY27 total income hit a record INR 236 crore, but PAT rose only 3% to INR 66 crore on a base effect from last year's write-backs and OLX tax.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was a record INR 213 crore, up 10% YoY and 6% QoQ, while EBITDA rose 20% YoY and 20% QoQ to INR 76 crore at a 36% margin. Other income fell sharply (OLX write-backs last year), and OLX tax rose after prior tax shelters, so PBT of INR 85 crore (up 7%) and PAT of INR 66 crore (up 3%) grew far slower than revenue. Management attributed the consumer group's slowdown (revenue +4%) mainly to a base effect from the September 2025 GST cut and a festive season that shifted into October and November, and guided Q3 to be the best quarter in company history.

financial_highlights.change: +20% YoY (INR 63.59 crore), +20% QoQ; margin 33% last year, 31% prior quarter

financial_highlights.value: Consumer/OLX other income INR 4.41 crore in OLX vs INR 13.51 crore last year
financial_highlights.change: Down; total other income down about 19% YoY in Q2 per management

financial_highlights.value: Over INR 1,400 crore as of 30 September 2026
76 million average (as stated) and 43 million monthly unique traffic (as asked by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited -18% YoY, -9% QoQ on 43 million figure; organic traffic 96%

segments.name: Consumer group (New Auto: CarWale, BikeWale)
segments.commentary: Revenue from operations +4% YoY, EBITDA +5%, margin 41%, PAT +13%; H1 revenue +10% and EBITDA +16%. Management attributed the slowdown to the high base of Q2 last year (37% growth in the quarter).

segments.name: Remarketing (SAMIL / Shriram Automall)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12% in the quarter and +13% half-yearly; EBITDA margin about 30% and PAT +47% in the quarter, driven by retail online auctions with the highest margins. Management said listed vehicles were about 1.56 million and auctioned about 2.35 lakh (annualised for Q2).

segments.name: OLX
segments.commentary: Revenue +26% YoY in the quarter and +28% half-yearly; EBITDA +36% with margin 32%; PAT declined on lower other income and 58% higher tax. Management guided growth to exceed 26% and reach 30-35% in coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 expected to be the best quarter in company history across most businesses, with highest-ever revenue; management declined to give a sequential growth rate for Q3.
Group EBITDA expected to grow sequentially at a similar rate (about 20%) from Q2 to Q3; management pointed to a path toward 40% group EBITDA margin.
OLX growth expected to exceed 26% and reach 30-35% in coming quarters, driven by existing products plus Elite Buyer, Elite Seller and e-commerce.
VAYA Live expected to roll out for OEMs/dealers and consumers sometime in the current quarter, becoming a flagship product over the next one to three quarters.
Long-term goal of about INR 1,000 crore PAT in four to five years, which management said is directionally on track.

No buyback or dividend possible this year under current regulation because the standalone tax benefit continues for one or two more years; cash to be used for M&A if found, otherwise distributions later.
capex_capacity: Management said the business is asset-light: no material capex and no meaningful working capital requirement, with most profits converting to cash.
VAYA tech costs described as largely fixed; no material change expected from VAYA rollout, with token and compute costs being optimised.
Landmark partnership for OLX car commerce: management is still working out whether CarTrade should invest part of working capital, depending on margin sharing.
Commerce platform with escrow and logistics for non-auto categories (mobiles, white goods) in product development; no date given beyond coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Management said there was no change in OEM vs dealer mix (about 65-70% OEM per earlier comment; CFO later said about 74% of consumer revenue from OEMs, up 3-4 points partly due to last year's timing).
Consumer revenue growth attributed to volume and conversion, not price escalation; lead generation is the largest revenue component.
Industry growth was concentrated in the September 2025 GST-cut period; management cited FADA data showing Navratri 2026 sales below last year's.

Traffic decline attributed to GST-related enthusiasm last year and the festive season shifting about 10 days into October; management said AI is not affecting genuine users and leads and organic share is 96%.
Management said online share of OEM spends is rising, with classifieds at about 18-20% of total OEM spend and a long runway vs 40-60% in developed markets.
OLX Elite Buyer launched about 30 days before the call with a 'massive uptake'; management declined to give an updated buyer count. Elite Seller is now a significant part of seller revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the consumer revenue slowdown is base effect or seasonality versus broader OEM ad-spend pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a complete base effect from the September 2025 GST cut, when Q2 last year grew 37%. It said OEM behaviour has not changed and that October 2026 would be the best month in New Auto history.

qa_highlights.question: Will OLX revenue growth accelerate, given product cadence?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said growth will exceed 26% and be stronger in the coming two quarters, driven mainly by existing products, with Elite Buyer, Elite Seller, Landmark car partnership and e-commerce adding later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise at OLX (about 15-16% QoQ) but fall about 12% in consumer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs were shifted: more investment in used cars at OLX and lower CarWale used-car management costs, since both businesses are common. It said the overall cost level is stable.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the standalone or consumer revenue is lead generation and what drives growth, volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead generation is the largest component. Growth comes from volume and conversion improvements, not rate escalations.

qa_highlights.question: Can cash be returned via buyback, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution is currently not permitted by regulation because the standalone tax benefit continues for one or two more years, so no buyback or dividend this year. Cash may go to M&A if a target is found.

qa_highlights.question: Will VAYA Live add material cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost is not material: it is built on AI code and proprietary data, avoiding LLM data costs, and the tech cost base is fixed.

risks_watch: Consumer group revenue growth (+4% YoY) and the depth of the base-effect recovery in Q3; management gave no numerical Q3 growth guidance.
Traffic: 43 million monthly unique visitors per the analyst's figure, down 18% YoY and 9% QoQ; watch whether festive-season traffic recovers in Q3.
Other income declines and OLX tax rates keep PAT growth lagging EBITDA; OLX PAT fell.
Opex trends: OLX employee cost rising sharply QoQ versus management's earlier statement that OpEx would be flat after Q1.
Landmark partnership economics, including any working capital investment and margin sharing, still under negotiation.
Capital return is constrained until the standalone tax benefit runs out; watch for buyback or dividend timing and any M&A.
VAYA Live and commerce product launches are promised within the quarter or in coming quarters; delivery is unproven.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the outlook, especially OLX and Q3 records, but defensive on the consumer slowdown and PAT growth, which management repeatedly attributed to base effects and tax. Evasive on quantified Q3 consumer growth, traffic guidance, and buyback timing.
key_quotes: We think it is a complete base effect. GST was lowered on 22nd September last year.
Q3 this year is likely to be our best ever quarter in almost all our businesses.
The tax shelters are actually gone in OLX and not in the standalone group.
We do not see really any impact of AI in users or genuine users.

growth.why: Management guided Q3 to be the best quarter ever with group EBITDA up about 20% QoQ and OLX growth crossing 30-35%, backed by Elite Buyer/Seller launches and VAYA Live, but gave no numeric revenue guidance and no capacity additions; asset-light model means no capex.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Group EBITDA margin was 36% in Q2 (31% prior quarter, 33% last year), and management guided EBITDA to grow about 20% QoQ again in Q3 with a path toward 40% group margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management described the business as asset-light with no material capex and no meaningful working capital need, so no physical capacity comes live in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consumer revenue grew only 4% YoY on a 37% high base and traffic fell 18% YoY to 43 million per the analyst's figure, while OLX revenue grew 26% with guidance of 30-35% and Q3 is guided as the best quarter ever.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says no material capex is needed; the only possible investment is working capital for the Landmark OLX partnership, still under negotiation with no number given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided Q3 to be the best quarter in company history and group EBITDA up about 20% QoQ, but gave no numeric revenue guidance, so an upgrade is conditional on festive-season recovery.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consumer revenue growth is only +4% YoY, Navratri 2026 sales were below last year per FADA, and OLX employee costs rose about 15-16% QoQ against earlier flat-opex comments.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: VAYA Live is expected to roll out in the current quarter and become a flagship over one to three quarters, and Elite Buyer launched about 30 days before the call; commerce platform for non-auto categories is in development with no date.

rows.label: OLX growth acceleration to 30-35%
rows.why: OLX revenue grew 26% YoY in Q2 and +28% half-yearly, and management guided growth above 26% and to 30-35% in coming quarters, driven by Elite Buyer, Elite Seller and Landmark.

rows.label: No buyback or dividend this year
rows.why: Regulation bars distributions while the standalone tax benefit runs one or two more years, so cash of over INR 1,400 crore goes to M&A if found, otherwise later.

rows.label: Consumer segment base-effect recovery
rows.why: Consumer revenue grew 4% YoY in Q2 against a 37% high base; management says October 2026 will be the best month in New Auto history, but traffic is down 18% YoY per the analyst figure.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q3 records, OLX acceleration and VAYA Live, but defensive on the consumer slowdown and PAT lag, attributing them to base effects, tax and festive timing; analysts pressed on traffic decline, OLX cost growth and buyback timing.
